content.title: Texas knocked out by UCLA in women's basketball Final Four game
content.text: Published April 3, 2026 at 5:01 AM CDT Updated April 4, 2026 at 11:12 AM CDT The Texas Longhorns women's basketball team fell 51-44 in Friday's Final Four game against UCLA. The team's head coach, Vic Schaefer, said at the post-game news conference "this one will haunt me, as coach, probably till the day I die."Despite excelling on the court defensively, the Longhorns struggled to make shots against the Bruins. That included junior, first team All-American Madison Booker. Booker, who typically averages just over 19 points a game, scored six points against UCLA."I got a whole team of really good players," Schaefer said. "I have no idea why the good Lord picked tonight for us to not be able to make a shot. But that's just the hand we got dealt with."Despite the loss, Schaefer said he remains proud of his team."My kids played their guts out tonight," he said. "I'm so proud of them. I'm just disappointed we couldn't score a few more points."It was the second straight year that the Longhorns advanced to the NCAA tournament semi-final game. The last time that kind of back-to-back happened was in 1987 when the team was coached by the legendary Jody Conradt.Conradt remains the only coach to lead a Texas women's basketball team to a national championship. Her 1986 team went 34-0, becoming the first team in NCAA history to complete a perfect season.Schaefer was looking to change that in his sixth year leading the program. "They're certainly the best team I've had at Texas. No question," Schaefer said at a news conference after the team's 77-41 win over Michigan on Monday.Schaefer also praised the team's work ethic and chemistry, both on and off the court."They're playing for each other. They're having fun. We have really good leadership right now. This is what happens when you have all that come together," he said.
